niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
competitors_mentioned: Tara Brach and Jack Kornfield. It
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want deep personal reflection, a steady meditation habit, or a more explicitly spiritual path. Based on the course details available, these are good starting points:

### For shadow work
- **Catherine Liggett — Exploring the Shadow**: A five-week live Zoom course with weekly exercises and group discussion. Its themes include emotional triggers, family patterns, body image, sexuality, money, and personal power. The intimate, emotionally intensive format may suit someone who wants structure and discussion; check when the next session runs and what support is available.
- **Shadow Work On Demand — Candace Van Dell**: A self-paced, 12-week course with video lessons, assignments, and guided meditations. The listed price is **$797**, so review the syllabus, instructor background, refund terms, and support options before enrolling.
- **Shadow Work Made Simple**: A self-paced course organized into 10 chapters, with a suggested completion window of roughly six to 12 weeks. It may be a more flexible option, though I’d compare its curriculum and instructor qualifications with your needs before buying.

### For spiritual practice and meditation
- **Mindfulness Daily — Tara Brach and Jack Kornfield**: A **free 40-day guided training** designed to help establish a regular mindfulness practice. A strong low-commitment place to begin.
- **Rice University — Mindfulness and Well-being**: Self-paced courses that combine meditation, reflection, and practical exercises. The Foundations course is a broad introduction; *Peace In, Peace Out* focuses more explicitly on mindfulness as spiritual development. The listed options include free auditing and a paid subscription.
- **Mindworks — Journey to Well-Being**: A progressive, self-paced mindfulness program grounded in Buddhist wisdom but presented without requiring Buddhist terminology or religious commitment. Its introductory level is free.
- **Sounds True courses**: A broad catalog of spiritual and contemplative programs, including offerings by experienced teachers such as Tara Brach and Jack Kornfield. It’s worth choosing a specific course based on your tradition and goals rather than treating the catalog as one uniform program.

**A sensible path:** Start with the free Mindfulness Daily or Mindworks introductory material, then add a shadow-work course if you want focused self-inquiry. Shadow work can bring up difficult emotions; choose a course that encourages pacing and boundaries, and consider working with a licensed mental-health professional if you’re dealing with trauma or significant distress. Course prices and schedules can change, so verify them on the provider’s site.

Sources: [Catherine Liggett](https://www.catherineliggett.com/shadowwork101) · [Shadow Work On Demand](https://shadowwork.candacevandell.com/od/) · [Shadow Work Made Simple FAQ](https://www.shadowwork.online/pages/faqs) · [Tara Brach courses](https://www.tarabrach.com/online-courses/) · [Rice University mindfulness courses](https://online.rice.edu/courses/mindfulness-and-well-being-foundations-meditation) · [Mindworks](https://mindworks.org/meditation-courses/mindfulness-courses/) · [Sounds True](https://www.soundstrue.com/)
